He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama Crimson Tide]]. In January 2017, Sexton was selected as a [[2017 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|McDonald's All-American]].{{Cite web |last=Stephens |first=Mitch |date=January 15, 2017 |title=2017 McDonald's All-American Game boys rosters announced |url=http://www.maxpreps.com/news/-c4H_udHpk68Wy2LGvrS3Q/2017-mcdonald’s-all-american-game-boys-rosters-announced.htm |access-date=February 20, 2017 |work=MaxPreps}} Nicknamed the "'''Young Bull'''",{{cite web|author=Ben Axelrod|url=https://www.wkyc.com/article/sports/nba/cavaliers/collin-sexton-shows-why-hes-nicknamed-young-bull-in-cleveland-cavaliers-summer-league/95-574666627|title=Collin Sexton shows why he's nicknamed 'Young Bull' in Cleveland Cavaliers' Summer League|publisher=[[WKYC]]|date=July 17, 2018|accessdate=May 7, 2021}}{{cite web|author=Sam Gordon|url=https://www.reviewjournal.com/sports/basketball/nba-summer-league/cavs-rookie-collin-sexton-embodies-nickname-on-the-court/|title=Cavs rookie Collin Sexton embodies nickname on the court|publisher=[[Las Vegas Review-Journal]]|date=July 11, 2018|accessdate=May 7, 2021}} he was selected with the 8th overall pick in the [[2018 NBA draft]] by the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]]. After spending his first 4 seasons with the team, he was traded to the [[Utah Jazz]] via sign-and-trade in the 2022 offseason. Sexton has also played for the [[Charlotte Hornets]]. ==Early life== Collin is the son of Darnell and Gia Sexton. He has an older brother, Jordan, and one older sister, Giuana. He started playing basketball when he was three years old.{{cite web |title=Collin Sexton |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/edge/basketball/nba/player/30579/collin-sexton |website=nbcsports.com |access-date=May 18, 2021 |archive-date=May 18, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210518160926/https://www.nbcsports.com/edge/basketball/nba/player/30579/collin-sexton |url-status=dead }} Collin first attended [[Hillgrove High School]] in [[Powder Springs, Georgia]] before transferring to [[Pebblebrook High School]] in [[Mableton, Georgia]] prior to his junior year and helped the Falcons to a 2016 Georgia Region 3-6A title and the 2016 Georgia Class 6A state championship game; while averaging 23 points, 7.4 rebounds and 2.9 assists.{{cite web |title=Collin Sexton - USA Basketball |url=https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/s/sexton-collin.aspx |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160611100707/http://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/s/sexton-collin.aspx |url-status=dead |archive-date=June 11, 2016 |website=usab.com |access-date=April 26, 2020}} Sexton was rated as a five-star recruit and considered one of the best players in the 2017 recruiting class by [[Scout.com]], [[Rivals.com]] and [[ESPN]].{{Cite web|url=https://247sports.com/Player/Collin-Sexton-89069|title=Collin Sexton, Cleveland Cavaliers, Point Guard}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/216120/collin-sexton|title=Collin Sexton - Basketball Recruiting - Player Profiles - ESPN}} Sexton was ranked as the No.7 overall recruit and No.2 point guard in the 2017 high school class.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/216120/collin-sexton|title=Collin Sexton – Basketball Recruiting – Player Profiles|work=ESPN.com|access-date=April 18, 2017}} On November 10, 2016, Sexton committed to the [[Alabama Crimson Tide]], on the same day he signed his letter of intent (LOI).{{cite news |last1=Sugiura |first1=Ken |title=Pebblebrook's Collin Sexton picks Alabama over Tech |url=https://www.ajc.com/sports/college/pebblebrook-collin-sexton-picks-alabama-over-tech/hX3Ix8QUlvEVUhZiHkvSEJ/ |access-date=July 17, 2018 |publisher=The Atlanta Journal-Constitution |date=November 10, 2016}} {{College athlete recruit start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2017}} {{College athlete recruit entry | recruit = Collin Sexton | position = [[Point guard|PG]] | hometown = [[Mableton, Georgia|Mableton, GA]] | highschool = [[Pebblebrook High School|Pebblebrook]] (GA) | feet = 6 | inches = 3 | weight = 175 | 40 = | commitdate = November 10, 2016 | scout stars = 5 | rivals stars = 5 | 247 stars = 5 | espn stars = 5 | espn grade = 95 }} {{College athlete recruit end | 40 = | year = 2017 | rivals ref title = Alabama 2017 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = 2017 Alabama Basketball Commits | espn ref title = 2017 Alabama Crimson Tide Recruiting Class | 247 ref title = 2017 Alabama 24/7 Sports Commits | rivals school = Alabama | 247 school = Alabama | scout s = Alabama | espn schoolid = | scout overall = #6 | rivals overall = #7 | 247 overall = #3 | espn overall = #7 | accessdate = September 6, 2016 | bball = yes }} ==College career== [[File:20170329 MCDAAG Collin Sexton dribbling across court.jpg|thumb|upright=0.85|Sexton in 2017]] Collin Sexton attended the [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|University of Alabama]], playing for coach [[Avery Johnson]]. On November 25, 2017, he scored 40 points while playing shorthanded (3-on-5) during most of the second half in a loss to the University of Minnesota.{{cite web|title=Live: Stadium College Basketball|url=https://www.facebook.com/StadiumCollegeBasketball/videos/780143202172438/|work=[[Facebook]]|access-date=November 25, 2017}}{{cite web|title=Alabama plays 10-plus minutes with 3 players after ejections, fouls, injury|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/21558686/alabama-finishes-game-3-players-entire-bench-ejected-scuffle|publisher=[[ESPN]]|access-date=January 3, 2018|first=Myron|last=Medcalf|date=November 26, 2017}} In the opening game of the [[SEC men's basketball tournament|SEC tournament]], Collin Sexton scored 27 points against [[Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball|Texas A&M]] including the game winning buzzer-beater, then 31 points in a quarterfinal win over #1 seed [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]], and 21 points against [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] in a loss during the semifinals. Collin Sexton was named to the All-tournament team after averaging 26.3 ppg, 3 apg, and 5 rpg in 3 games. Following Alabama's loss in the [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2018 NCAA men's basketball tournament]], Sexton announced his intention to forgo his final three seasons of collegiate eligibility and declare for the [[2018 NBA draft]], where he was expected to be a first round selection.{{Cite news|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/nba-draft-2018-alabama-freshman-collin-sexton-declares-for-the-draft-and-could-be-a-lottery-pick/|title=Alabama freshman Collin Sexton declares for the draft|work=[[CBS Sports]]|date=April 6, 2018}} ===FBI investigation=== {{main|2017 NCAA Division I men's basketball corruption scandal}} Before Alabama's exhibition game on November 6, 2017, the school announced that Sexton would not play due to eligibility concerns. These concerns stemmed from Alabama's director of basketball operations Kobie Baker's resignation, following an internal investigation after the announcement of an FBI investigation into college basketball corruption.{{Cite news|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/sec/2017/11/06/alabama-freshman-point-guard-collin-sexton-not-eligible-ncaa-exhibition/838454001/|title=Alabama freshman point guard Collin Sexton not eligible, missed exhibition game|work=USA TODAY|access-date=November 7, 2017|language=en}} Sexton would, however, make his debut with Alabama on November 14 in a win against [[Lipscomb University]]. Later on in February 2018, Sexton's name would pop up as one of the names implicated with the NCAA scandal of receiving payments or dinners. His name was once again cleared. ==Professional career== ===Cleveland Cavaliers (2018–2022)=== On June 21, 2018, Sexton was selected with the eighth overall pick by the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in the [[2018 NBA draft]]. The Cavaliers had acquired the Nets' pick from the Celtics via the [[Kyrie Irving]] trade the previous summer, who had acquired it initially in 2014 as part of the blockbuster trade of Paul Pierce and Kevin Garnett, among others.{{refn|group=upper-alpha|name=FromBostonToCleveland|July 12, 2013: [[Brooklyn Nets]] to [[Boston Celtics]]{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press_release/celtics-complete-trade-brooklyn-nets|title=Celtics Complete Trade With Brooklyn Nets|date=July 12, 2013|work=NBA.com|access-date=May 19, 2016}} *Boston acquired [[Gerald Wallace]], [[Kris Humphries]], [[Keith Bogans]], [[MarShon Brooks]], [[Kris Joseph]], a 2014 first-round pick, a 2016 first-round pick, the option to swap 2017 first-round picks, and ''a 2018 first-round pick'' *Brooklyn acquired [[Paul Pierce]], [[Kevin Garnett]], [[Jason Terry]] and [[D. J. White]]; Brooklyn also acquired Boston's 2017 second-round pick for compensation after the 2015–16 season ended. August 30, 2017: [[Boston Celtics]] to [[Cleveland Cavaliers]]{{cite web|title=Celtics Acquire Four-Time All-Star Kyrie Irving|url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-acquire-four-time-all-star-kyrie-irving|work=NBA.com|date=August 22, 2017|access-date=August 22, 2017}}{{cite web|last=Wojnarowski|first=Adrian|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/20512119/cleveland-cavaliers-getting-additional-2020-second-rounder-boston-celtics-complete-trade|title=Cavs add 2nd-round pick from Celtics to complete Kyrie Irving-Isaiah Thomas trade|work=ESPN.com|date=August 30, 2017|access-date=August 30, 2017}} *Cleveland acquired [[Isaiah Thomas (basketball)|Isaiah Thomas]], [[Jae Crowder]], [[Ante Žižić]], ''the Brooklyn Nets' 2018 first-round pick'', and the Miami Heat's 2020 second-round pick (latter pick added as compensation for Thomas' failed physical) *Boston acquired [[Kyrie Irving]]}} He was the highest-selected player from Alabama since [[Antonio McDyess]] in [[1995 NBA draft|1995]]. On July 6, 2018, Sexton made his [[NBA Summer League]] debut. He recorded 15 points to go along with 7 rebounds.{{cite news |last1=Inabinett |first1=Mark |title=Collin Sexton makes pro debut in NBA Summer League |url=https://www.al.com/sports/index.ssf/2018/07/collin_sexton_makes_pro_debut.html |access-date=July 17, 2018 |publisher=The Birmingham News |date=July 7, 2018}} On October 17, 2018, Sexton made his NBA debut, coming off the bench for the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] with nine points and three rebounds in a 104–116 loss to the [[Toronto Raptors]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070698|title=Newcomer Kawhi Leonard scores 24 as Raptors beat Cavaliers|date=October 17, 2018|work=ESPN.com|access-date=October 17, 2018}} On November 24, 2018, Sexton scored a season-high 29 points against the [[Houston Rockets]] in a 117–108 victory. On December 9, 2018, he again scored 29 points against the [[Washington Wizards]] in a 116–101 victory.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com.au/nba/recap?gameId=401071062|title=Wizards vs. Cavaliers - Game Recap - December 9, 2018 - ESPN|website=ESPN.com|language=en|access-date=January 22, 2019}} On March 8, 2019, Sexton passed [[Kyrie Irving]] for 3 pointers made as a Cavs rookie with 76 against the [[Miami Heat]]. He also eclipsed 1,000 career points. On March 11, 2019, Sexton had 28 points against the [[Toronto Raptors]] in a 126–101 victory, to go along with 5 assists and 4 rebounds. In the week of March 8, 2019, Sexton had the best week of his rookie campaign, averaging 26.0 points, 3.8 assists, and 2.5 rebounds. During a stretch from March 8 to 22, he became the first rookie to score 23+ points in seven consecutive games since Tim Duncan in 1998, as well the only rookie in franchise history to successively score at least 23 points. Additionally, he is the only rookie in NBA history to have played at least 2,000 minutes while scoring over 16 points per game on over 40% 3-point accuracy and fewer than 3 turnovers. He was named to the [[Rising Stars Challenge|Rising Stars Game]] at the [[2020 NBA All-Star Game|2020 NBA All-Star Weekend]] as a replacement for injured Miami Heat rookie [[Tyler Herro]],{{Cite web|last=release|first=Official|title=Cavaliers' Collin Sexton to replace Heat's Tyler Herro in 2020 NBA Rising Stars|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2020/02/11/collin-sexton-replaces-tyler-hero-rising-stars-official-release|access-date=June 13, 2020|website=NBA.com|language=en}} where he put up 21 points, 5 rebounds and 3 assists{{Cite web|title=World vs. USA - Box Score - February 14, 2020 - ESPN|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=401197814|access-date=June 13, 2020|website=ESPN.com|language=en}} for Team USA. On March 4, 2020, Sexton scored a season-high 41 points, alongside three rebounds and six assists, in a 106–112 loss to the [[Boston Celtics]].{{Cite web |title=TATUM SCORES 32, LEADS CELTICS PAST CAVALIERS 112-106 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021900917 |access-date=February 1, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} He led the Cavaliers in points per game (20.8) during the 2019–20 season, and also joined [[LeBron James]] and [[Kyrie Irving]] as the only Cavaliers to average at least 20 points per game before turning 22 years old.{{Cite web |title=Collin Sexton Season In Review: Gloom And Doom Or Slap Happy Hooray? |url=https://cavsnation.com/collin-sexton-season-in-review-gloom-and-doom-or-slap-happy-hooray |access-date=February 1, 2023 |website=Cavs Nation}}{{Cite web |title=Cleveland Cavaliers 2019-20 Season Preview, Revisited |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/evandammarell/2020/03/17/cleveland-cavaliers-2019-20-season-preview-revisited/?sh=25f0e1c665fc |access-date=February 1, 2023 |work=Forbes}} Sexton scored at least 25 points in seven of his last eight games of the season, the longest such streak since James did so during his stint in Cleveland.{{Cite web |title=2019-20 Season Recap: Cleveland Cavaliers |url=https://www.nba.com/2019-20-season-reset-cavs |access-date=February 1, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} [[File:Collin Sexton (44559770794).jpg|upright=0.85|thumb|Sexton in 2018]] On January 20, 2021, Sexton set a new career high of 42 points in a 147–135 double overtime win against the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web |title=Cavaliers' Collin Sexton: Generates new career high |url=https://www.cleveland.com/cavs/2021/01/cavaliers-past-meets-present-and-future-as-collin-sexton-bests-kyrie-irving-brooklyn-nets-in-147-135-win.html |website=cleveland.com |access-date=January 21, 2021 |date=January 21, 2021}} During the 2020–21 campaign, Sexton led the Cavaliers in scoring for a second straight year with a career-high 24.3 points per game, and also set a career high with 4.4 assists per game.{{Cite web |title=Collin Sexton 2020-21 Season Review |url=https://www.fearthesword.com/2021/7/2/22559074/collin-sexton-2020-21-season-review |access-date=February 2, 2023 |website=SB Nation}}{{Cite web |title=Cleveland Cavaliers Season Recap |url=https://primetimesportstalk.com/2021/05/31/cleveland-cavaliers-season-recap/ |access-date=February 2, 2023 |work=Prime Time Sports Talk}} Sexton and the Cavaliers failed to reach an agreement on a contract extension before the 2021–22 season started.{{Cite web |title=Cavaliers, Sexton fail to reach contract extension; Sexton can be restricted free agent after season |url=https://www.cleveland.com/cavs/2021/10/cleveland-cavaliers-collin-sexton-fail-to-reach-contract-extension-agreement-sexton-can-become-restricted-free-agent-following-season.html |access-date=February 2, 2023 |website=Cleveland.com}} On October 22, 2021, he scored a season-high 33 points, alongside four rebounds and two steals, in a 112–123 loss to the [[Charlotte Hornets]].{{Cite web |title=BRIDGES SCORES 30 POINTS, HORNETS BEAT CARELESS CAVS 123-112 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022100017 |access-date=February 2, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} On November 7, Sexton exited a road game against the [[New York Knicks]] with a knee injury, which was later revealed to be a torn left meniscus. There was no timetable set for his return.{{cite web |date=November 8, 2021 |title=Cleveland Cavaliers guard Collin Sexton has meniscus tear |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/32584787/cleveland-cavaliers-guard-collin-sexton-meniscus-tear |access-date=November 8, 2021 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press}} On November 20, it was revealed that he had season-ending surgery.{{Cite web|title=Report: Cavs' Collin Sexton Out for Season After Undergoing Surgery on Knee Injury|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10017605-report-cavs-collin-sexton-out-for-season-after-undergoing-surgery-on-knee-injury|url-status=live|access-date=November 19, 2021|website=Bleacher Report|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211120021639/https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10017605-report-cavs-collin-sexton-out-for-season-after-undergoing-surgery-on-knee-injury |archive-date=November 20, 2021 }} On June 28, 2022, the Cavaliers extended a qualifying offer to Sexton, making him a [[restricted free agent]].{{Cite web |title=Cavaliers extend qualifying offer to Collin Sexton |url=https://www.nba.com/news/cavaliers-extend-qualifying-offer-to-collin-sexton |access-date=February 2, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} === Utah Jazz (2022–2025) === On September 3, 2022, Sexton was [[Sign-and-trade deal|signed-and-traded]], alongside [[Lauri Markkanen]], [[Ochai Agbaji]], three future first-round picks, and two future pick swaps, to the [[Utah Jazz]] in exchange for [[Donovan Mitchell]]. As part of the deal, Sexton agreed to a four-year, $72 million contract with the Jazz.{{Cite web |title=Cavs Acquire Three-Time All-Star Donovan Mitchell |url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/releases-mitchell-trade-220903 |access-date=September 3, 2022 |website=NBA}}{{Cite web |last=Wojnarowski |first=Adrian |author-link=Adrian Wojnarowski |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/34502825/sources-cleveland-cavaliers-trade-3-first-round-picks-two-swaps-utah-jazz-star-donovan-mitchell |access-date=2025-03-09 |website=ESPN.com}} Sexton made his debut for the Jazz on October 19, recording 20 points, 5 rebounds, and 2 assists while coming off the bench in a 123–102 win over the [[Denver Nuggets]].{{Cite web |title=NEW-LOOK JAZZ BEAT NUGGETS 123-102 IN SEASON OPENER |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022200012 |access-date=January 22, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} ===Charlotte Hornets (2025–2026)=== On June 29, 2025, Sexton was traded to Lakers (2026–present)=== On July 12, 2026, Sexton signed a two-year, $19-million contract with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite news|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/lakers/2026/07/12/los-angeles-lakers-collin-sexton-nba-free-agency/90894911007/|title=Los Angeles Lakers officially announce Collin Sexton signing|website=USA Today|date=July 12, 2026|first=Andrés|last=Soto}} ==National team career== Sexton won a gold medal with the 2016 USA Men's U17 World Championship Team, at the [[2016 FIBA Under-17 World Championship]] in Zaragoza, Spain. He was [[FIBA Under-17 Basketball World Cup Most Valuable Player|named the MVP of the tournament]]. ==Personal life== Sexton was born in [[Marietta, Georgia]], and grew up in [[Mableton, Georgia]] with his mother and father, Gia and Darnell Sexton, and his brother, Jordan Sexton.{{cite web|url=https://www.wvtm13.com/article/mom-brother-proud-of-alabama-star-collin-sexton/19389606|title=Mom,
